projects.name: HIVE
projects.summary: A CroLabs framework that onboards different robots from their own code and coordinates them through a shared world model.
projects.description: HIVE — Heterogeneous Intelligent Vehicle Ensemble — lets one plain-language mission drive a mixed team of ground, aerial, and manipulator robots. Onboarding reads a robot's ROS 2 workspace, collects interface evidence, and drafts a capability profile for human review. Each reviewed robot becomes an embodied agent; an Executive plans against a shared world model and dispatches validated steps, while navigation, flight, manipulation, and emergency stop stay on the robot.
highlights: Code-first onboarding: a robot's ROS 2 workspace becomes a structured capability profile — skills, interfaces, limits — that a human reviews before use.
Embodied agents expose only reviewed capabilities, so the Executive never assigns a robot a task it can't perform.
Safety-critical control stays local: the Executive coordinates tasks, and each robot keeps its own navigation, flight, manipulation, and stop logic.

projects.name: Amphibious robot
projects.summary: Structure and packaging for a CroLabs ring-frame robot designed to fly, drive, and swim.
projects.description: A CroLabs team robot built around four ring frames with enclosed propellers and a central electronics bay, designed to move through air, over ground, and through water with a single airframe. My part is the structure: the frame layout, component packaging, and the laser-cut frame that carries thrust, ground, and water loads.

facts.label: frame materials compared in the trade study

highlights: Four ring frames enclose the propellers and tie into a laser-cut central structure.
Compute and power electronics sit in a central bay between the four rings.
A frame-material trade study ranks six sheet materials on stiffness and strength per weight, water durability, impact toughness, and in-house manufacturability.

projects.name: Drone Tracker · compact quadcopter
projects.summary: A palm-sized ducted quadcopter designed to follow a subject with GPS and film from a tilt gimbal — CAD, packaging, and frame FEA in Fusion 360.
projects.description: Drone Tracker is a roughly 140 mm cinewhoop-style quadcopter designed around a SpeedyBee F7 Mini running Betaflight, a Be-180 GPS for follow and position hold, ELRS radio control, and a camera on a single-axis tilt gimbal. Its CINEC 25.1.2 ducted frame was analyzed in Fusion 360 Simulation under a 400 g total-thrust load case: peak von Mises stress was 1.96 MPa, and the ducts and prop guards turned out to carry load alongside the frame rather than only protecting the props.

facts.label: peak von Mises stress, 400 g thrust case
parts in the bill of materials

highlights: Static FEA in carbon fiber: central top deck fixed, four upward 0.98 N loads at the motor bells, 1.33 million tetrahedral elements.
A frame-only baseline showed much higher peak stress than the full assembly — the ducts and prop guards are primary load-sharing members.
Every flight-controller port is assigned: GPS on UART2, ELRS on UART3, VTX control on UART4, gimbal servo on PWM5.
Impact loading is the next analysis case.

projects.name: Natural-language robotic arm
projects.summary: Speak or type a command, and a language agent turns it into pick-and-place on a simulated 7-DOF Franka Panda.
projects.description: Hold the mic button and say “put the green box on the shelf,” or type it. faster-whisper transcribes speech locally on the CPU, a local parser handles common phrasing, and NVIDIA NIM tool calling resolves ambiguous requests. The agent sequences look, find, pick, and place skills, and mink differential IK drives a 7-DOF Franka Panda in MuJoCo. Object poses come from simulator state, and grasps use a weld constraint.

facts.label: colored objects to pick and place

highlights: Local push-to-talk speech: 2.6 s of speech transcribed in 0.53 s on a CPU, with no cloud speech service.
Transcripts that are too short, low-confidence, or known Whisper hallucinations are dropped before they reach the arm.
Scene and wrist camera views answer questions about the scene through NIM vision.

projects.name: ROS 2 micromouse
projects.summary: A ROS 2 flood-fill planner that drives the mms micromouse simulator and a Gazebo robot in lockstep.
projects.description: One flood-fill solution drives two simulators at once. A generated 16 × 16 maze feeds the planner, which computes a distance field over the maze and walks the gradient to the goal. Moves go to the mms interface over its text protocol and, through a ROS 2 cell-motion controller, to a Gazebo Harmonic robot that mirrors each step with exact pose updates.
highlights: Planning logic is decoupled from both simulators through ROS 2 topics.
Unit tests cover maze generation, the flood-fill gradient, the mms file format, and planner tie-breaking.
Plans on a known maze; Gazebo follows each cell move with exact pose updates.

projects.name: Jarvis · agent orchestrator
projects.summary: A local-first assistant on OpenJarvis that routes each task to the right model, convenes a planning council for hard problems, and calls tools over MCP.
projects.description: Jarvis is built on OpenJarvis (Apache-2.0), vendored unmodified. My work is the integration layer: a FastAPI sidecar that wires routing, a planning council, a user-drawn agent graph, memory, MCP tools, and voice into the OpenJarvis LiteLLM engine. Every model call takes one path with a fallback ladder — an NVIDIA NIM model, a second NIM model, Gemini Flash, then local Ollama.

facts.label: rungs in the model fallback ladder
web tests, network and LLM calls mocked

highlights: Fallback ladder with exponential backoff and rate-limit handling across NIM, Gemini, and local Ollama.
Three-model planning council: parallel proposals, a reasoning-model critique, one synthesized plan.
A 174-test web suite covers the sidecar, router, council, graph, memory, voice, vision, and tools, with network, LLM, and camera calls mocked.

projects.name: Robot learning with ACT
projects.summary: A reproducible LeRobot ACT training pipeline on SO-101 data, with a 10,000-step run and verified checkpoint reload.
projects.description: A locked LeRobot 0.5.0 environment on WSL2 trained an Action Chunking Transformer for 10,000 steps on the public SO-101 pick-and-place dataset, then reloaded the checkpoint in a fresh process and ran GPU inference. Two 80-episode simulated SO-101 datasets in LeRobot v3 format, recorded in MuJoCo with a scripted expert, are ready for the next stage. The work was paused in September 2026 before task-success evaluation.
highlights: 10,000 of 10,000 training steps completed, exit code 0.
Checkpoint reload and GPU inference verified in a separate process.
Two scripted-expert MuJoCo datasets: 8,083 and 7,794 frames at 30 fps.
